sourceBlockers.detail: Unlabeled volumes expose no durable physical-instance identity. Name-based lookup is not ownership. Backup still fails closed; witnessed adoption is not implemented. A StateStore adoption record needs independently observed physical identity and canonical ownership, without asserting creation freshness. Backend creation timestamp alone must not authorize restore after same-name recreation.

Missing seed state still defaults to fresh for a known instance. Creation-time freshness evidence is not persisted by the creator. This does not satisfy the acceptance criterion; the fake's explicit fresh status is not live creation evidence.

Snapshot version is derived from the current plan, not an observed database version. Restart still calls the provider with the current plan. Exact inspected-runtime resumption under edited configuration remains unproved.

Volume creation labels do not bind the planner canonical owner key. SQL now rechecks instance identity inside its lock, but this does not establish ownership of unknown name collisions or prove that every lifecycle/removal writer shares the lock.

MySQL/MariaDB dump commands still lack consistent-read flags. PR966 was inspected read-only and overlaps this file plus families.test.ts and run.test.ts. Its flags were not applied here; the PR was not modified.
